question: Should OpenClaw accept a bundled 1Password SecretRef provider that reads a plugin-held service-account token and passes it to a locally installed, permission-validated op executable, including its new plugin-local dependency?
rationale: The patch is not a mechanical bug fix: it establishes a privileged secret-resolution trust boundary and changes the resolved dependency graph, both of which require repository-owner acceptance beyond contributor proof.

options.title: Approve the managed provider boundary
options.body: Authorize the exact dependency graph and accept the plugin-owned op executable validation model after security review of the supported-platform behavior.

options.title: Keep only the existing broker
options.body: Decline the managed SecretRef surface and retain the current curated agent broker plus manual exec-provider configuration.

options.title: Request a narrower external integration path
options.body: Ask for a documented external provider/plugin route if maintainers do not want this capability bundled with core distribution.

recommendation.title: Approve the managed provider boundary
recommendation.body: Authorize the exact dependency graph and accept the plugin-owned op executable validation model after security review of the supported-platform behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the clearest merged-history connection to the existing SecretRef provider architecture, though final approval should come from the repository's responsible security/product reviewer.
